conventions.convention: Foundation-model status is qualitative, architecture-independent, and provides no numerical size threshold or downstream performance guarantee. In-context learning keeps pretrained parameters fixed.

Source and target laws share a measurable input/label product space. Conditional label kernels are supplied rather than asserted to exist; covariate shift additionally requires target-almost-everywhere kernel equality and target marginal absolute continuity with respect to the source marginal.

N excludes embedding parameters, D counts tokens, and the three loss fits apply separately in their specified training regimes and measured ranges. Empirical exponents do not imply capability or universal transfer guarantees.

The finite spaces carry power-set sigma-algebras, the source and target laws are point masses at (a,0) and (b,1), and parameter ERM is specified only for nonempty samples when its infimum is attained.

load_bearing.statement: In the usage of the 2021 Bommasani et al. report, a foundation model is a model trained on broad data, generally using self-supervision at scale, that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. The definition makes no general transfer, capability-emergence, or reliability claim from a pretraining loss.

concerns.concern: The Example gives “C_min=6NB_crit S” and defines S as “the number of training steps.” With actual steps S at batch size B, Kaplan et al. §5.1 equations (5.4)–(5.5) instead give S_min=S/(1+B_crit/B) and C_min=6NBS/(1+B/B_crit)=6NB_crit S_min. Thus the displayed equality is generally false with the stated unadjusted meaning of S. Although §6.1 of the paper itself writes the abbreviated formula reproduced here, the example needs to distinguish actual and adjusted step counts. Source checked: [Kaplan et al., §§5.1 and 6.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2001.08361).
